$comment: How AFC_Frontend meets owner rules R55 to R61 (2026-09-17). A Next.js client of the AFC-B API: no database, no paid service, no login handler of its own. Secrets never live here (R55); the API's ownership rules and their runtime IDOR cases live in AFC-B/security/. Read by ~/.claude/skills/security-rules/scripts/check-security.mjs.

allow.reason: not SQL: a next-intl message key built from the provider id (t.raw(`guides.${provider.id}.steps`)); nothing runs as a query or a command

tracked on purpose: it holds only NEXT_PUBLIC_* values (the API origin, the site origin, the Google client id, feature flags), which ship in the bundle anyway; a secret never goes here, .env.local is git-ignored for those

tracked on purpose and holds only NEXT_PUBLIC_* values (the API origin, the site origin, a Google OAuth client id, which is public by design, and two feature flags); git log -p over every commit of the file shows no other key ever in it (checked 2026-09-18); secrets live in .env.local, which is ignored

accepted by the owner 2026-10-04 (inbox #142, "accept it"): braces <=3.0.3 stack exhaustion on deeply nested patterns, high, with NO patched release yet (pnpm audit: patched <0.0.0). Its only path is the lint toolchain, eslint-config-next > @next/eslint-plugin-next > fast-glob > micromatch > braces; pnpm audit --prod lists no advisory at all, so it is not in the shipped site or the server, and the glob patterns it parses are our own lint config, never visitor input. Review on 2026-11-04 or as soon as a fixed braces (or a fast-glob / micromatch that drops it) is published, then upgrade and delete this line

not a request body: the how-to clips seed builds each demo event from a dict written in the file itself (tournament(name, slug, **extra) with literal fields) and runs only on the local clips database afc_howto (asserted on its first lines); no client ever reaches it

the how-to clips recorder puts a demo player's session token into its own throwaway headless Chrome, on localhost, the way the site's own code reads it (js-cookie, so it cannot be httpOnly there); no real session, no deployed page, the browser profile is deleted after each take

https.enforcedBy: nginx on the VPS, in the backend repo's deploy kit (AFC-B deploy/vps/nginx-afc.conf): port 80 answers 301 to https; HSTS max-age=31536000 includeSubDomains on the site and the API host; read back live 2026-09-18
